answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity stake work that is hard to fake at scale: an agent must post a small bond and build a reputation vertex, a public record of graded judgments tied to that one identity, before its votes count. Newcomers start at the lotus stage, low-trust and closely watched, and only graduate as their graded work accumulates. To forge dozens of fresh identities then costs real time and real stake per identity, so a sybil swarm cannot outvote a community that has already paid its dues.
